title: MEXT Special Needs Education Survey: Assistive Technology Diffusion, Resource Room Expansion, and Inclusion Bottlenecks in Japan
source_name: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
description: Annual institutional census of special needs education in Japan, evaluating the relational impact of assistive tablet technology, specialized resource room instruction (Tsukyu), and support staff allocation on mainstream classroom participation rates.
observation_unit: School stage panel tracking special needs service utilization across 5 survey cycles (2016-2024)
sample_population_note: Annual MEXT administrative survey of all public elementary and junior high schools in Japan
title_ja: 【特別支援教育実態調査】支援技術（ICT）の普及と通級指導・普通学級包摂率の多変量分析

research_angles.title: Assistive Technology as an Inclusion Catalyst: Disentangling Hardware Diffusion from Human Staffing Bottlenecks in Japanese Special Education
research_questions: To what degree does assistive tablet adoption facilitate mainstream classroom inclusion?
Does the shortage of certified specialized support personnel limit the efficacy of digital assistive technology?
hypotheses: Assistive technology adoption exhibits a statistically significant positive relationship with mainstream inclusion (VIF < 2.5).
Multiple regression reveals that specialized support staff ratio provides a crucial compounding effect necessary for sustained secondary inclusion.
research_angles.theoretical_framework: Universal Design for Learning (UDL) Framework and Social Model of Disability
